title: Blanquette de Veau
subtitle: French white veal stew with cream and mushrooms
excerpt: One of the glories of French bourgeois cooking: veal slowly simmered in a pale, ivory broth, the cooking liquid enriched with cream and egg yolk into a velvety sauce, with pearl onions and button mushrooms throughout. Rich, delicate, and deeply comforting.

recipe.sourceNotes: Blanquette de veau is one of the most beloved dishes of French home cooking, a pale, creamy veal stew that belongs to the tradition of dishes in white sauce (plats en sauce blanche). The blanquette technique starts with the meat in cold water which is brought to a simmer and skimmed; the meat is not browned, which would give colour and destroy the characteristic pale, ivory appearance. The stew is finished with a cream and egg yolk liaison (liaison à la crème) which thickens the sauce and gives it its characteristic rich, velvety texture. The liaison must not boil after it is added or the egg yolk will scramble and the sauce will curdle. The dish is traditionally served with boiled rice or steamed potatoes.

content.text: Do not brown the veal; the pale appearance is the defining characteristic of a blanquette. The cream and egg yolk liaison is added off the heat and must not boil afterwards, or the sauce will scramble. Taste for salt before adding the liaison as it is harder to adjust once the cream is in.

Place the veal in a large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil, drain, rinse the meat and the pot. Return to the pot with the onion, carrot, celery, bay, thyme, and salt. Cover with cold water and bring to a very gentle simmer. Poach for 60 to 75 minutes until very tender. Remove the meat. Strain and measure 600 ml of the cooking liquid.

Melt the butter in a saucepan. Add the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the 600 ml of reserved cooking liquid. Simmer for 10 minutes. Add the pearl onions and mushrooms and cook for 10 minutes more.

Beat the cream and egg yolks together. Remove the sauce from the heat. Stir in the cream liaison. Return the veal to the sauce. Heat very gently without boiling. Add the lemon juice. Adjust the seasoning and serve with boiled rice.
